## Port.getStdin() method

Get the input piped into this script.

**Signature:**

```typescript
getStdin(): NetscriptPort | null;
```
**Returns:**

[NetscriptPort](./bitburner.netscriptport.md) \| null

The script's stdin, or null if nothing was piped into it.

## Remarks

RAM cost: 0 GB

Returns a handle to this script's stdin, which holds anything piped into it from the terminal. For example, if the script was started with `echo input1 | run myScript.js`<!-- -->, then `ns.port.getStdin().read()` inside `myScript.js` returns `"input1"`<!-- -->. Returns null if nothing was piped into the script.

Data can keep arriving while the script runs, for example when another script's output is piped into it. Use `await stdin.nextWrite()` to wait for more data.

When the command piping into this script finishes, the stream is closed and `read()` returns `null` once. After that, `nextWrite()` resolves immediately, so stop reading when you get `null`<!-- -->. If the stream is empty but not closed, `read()` returns `"NULL PORT DATA"`<!-- -->, as with any other port.

## Example


```js
// echo "a b c" | run myScript.js
const stdin = ns.port.getStdin();
if (stdin === null) {
  ns.tprint("Nothing was piped into this script.");
  return;
}
while (true) {
  if (stdin.empty()) await stdin.nextWrite();
  const data = stdin.read();
  if (data === null) break; // The input has ended
  ns.tprint(data);
}
```
